title: India reach 10th successive final | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:49
-     - 5

India reached their 10th successive final of the Women’s Asia Cup when they defeated Bangladesh by 40 runs in the first semi-final played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium earlier this week. 

This is the 10th edition of the tournament and India has made it to the final in all of them thus underlying their dominance. They will meet Sri Lanka in the final.

It wasn’t easy for India, but they found a way to get close to the 150-run mark, and for that they had to thank Shafali Verma, who smashed seven fours and three sixes en route to her 20th fifty in WT20I cricket – a 64 off 40 deliveries. Bangladesh had only themselves to blame for they dropped her three times and also missed a straightforward run-out opportunity.

India lost Smriti Mandhana early, but Pratika Rawal and Verma put on 50 runs for the second wicket off 44 balls to steady the innings. It was Verma who kept the pressure on Bangladesh, taking the attack to them. Pratika scored 20 off 24, while Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 24 off 28 as they found it difficult to score at a brisk pace. Richa Ghosh (21 off 16) and Deepti Sharma (13 off 6) chipped in with useful cameos in the latter half to ensure India didn’t lose momentum. Run-scoring had been tough on this slow pitch, as Bangladesh was to find out later in their innings.

title: Sri Lanka reach seventh Asia Cup final | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:49
-     - 4

Defending champions Sri Lanka reached their seventh Women’s Asia Cup final when they beat Pakistan by four wickets with eight balls to spare in a closely contested second semi-final played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium yesterday.

Sri Lanka will meet seven-times champions India in the final on Sunday.

Set a target of 131 Sri Lanka stumbled to 33-4 with Pakistan captain Fatima Sana leading the way with a double wicket first over. A 67-run stand for the fifth wicket between Harshitha Samarawickrama (36) and Imesha Dulani (33) brought Sri Lanka back into contention.

But Sana had not finished yet for when she came for a second spell she once again struck twice to send back both set batters. However the experienced Nilakshika Silva (18*) and Kaushini Nuthyangana (10*) kept cool heads to see Sri Lanka over the line.   

Sana led Pakistan from the front and guided her team to 130 after being invited to bat first. Pakistan lost Muneeba Ali early, but Shawaal Zulfiqar and Gull Feroza then chipped in with scores in the 20s. Pakistan were 92-5 at the end of 16 overs when Tuba Hassan joined Sana, and the duo put on an all-important unbeaten 38-run stand off just 24 deliveries. Sana scored 47 off 36 balls and made sure Pakistan touched the 130-run mark. She took the Player of the Match award for her superb all-round contribution.

Scores: 

Pakistan Women 130-5 (20) (Shawaal Zulfiqar 24, Gull Feroza 21, Fatima Sana 47*, Chamari Athapaththu 2/24, Chamudi Praboda 2/25) lost to Sri Lanka Women 134-6 (18.4) (Imesh Dulani 24, Harshitha Samarawickrama 36, Kavisha Dilhari 33, Fatima Sana 4/38)

title: Sonal Dinusha in men’s shortlist for ICC Player of the Month award | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:48
-     - 4

Sonal Dinusha

Sri Lanka batter Sonal Dinusha, England pace bowler Ollie Robinson and Bangladesh fast bowler Hasan Mahmud feature on the men’s shortlist for the ICC Player of the Month award for August, while Thailand’s Suleeport Laomi and Nannapat Koncharoenkai are in contention for the women’s honour alongside Lucy Barnett, who becomes the first player from the Isle of Man to make the shortlist.

The three players in the race for the men’s award this time have impactful performances in Test cricket. Dinusha was the find of the home series against India, Robinson continued his outstanding efforts in home conditions against Pakistan and Hasan helped his team to a historic win on Australian soil.

The women’s shortlist shines the spotlight on Associate players who have delivered standout performances on the international stage. Laomi and Koncharoenkai boast performances in ODIs and T20Is including the ongoing Women’s Asia Cup in Dubai while Barnett excelled in the Continental Cup in Romania.

On Dinusha, the ICC had this to say of his nomination:  “Dinusha was resolute in the ICC World Test Championship series against India, belying his experience of only three previous Tests. The 25-year-old left-hander amassed 420 runs including scores of 100 and 84 in the first Test in Galle that his team lost and produced scores of 103 and 133 not out to save the next Test in Colombo, becoming only the third batter in the history of the game to score twin-centuries for a team that was made to follow on.”

summary:

Shaakib Zumri

Fourth-year Coloursman and 2026 Isipathana College first XV rugby captain, Shaakib Zumri has been named skipper of the Colombo ACES for the inaugural Next XV Rugby Tournament, which gets underway on 19 September at the CR and FC Grounds, Longden Place.

The talented Number Eight has enjoyed an outstanding school rugby career and will lead one of the tournament’s strongest outfits. Zumri was a key member of Isipathana’s President’s Trophy knockout championship-winning teams in both 2024 and 2025 before taking over the captaincy this season.

Earlier this year, he inspired Isipathana to the Zahira Invitational Rugby Sevens title with a series of impressive performances. His powerful ball carrying, defensive work and leadership qualities have made him one of the leading schoolboy forwards in the country.

Zumri also represented Sri Lanka at the 2024 Asia Rugby Under-18 Sevens Championship in Malaysia. Following his school career, he is expected to join CR and FC for the 2026/27 club rugby season.

Zumri will have Chinchi (Zahira) and Nisith (Trinity) as his two deputy skippers for this tournament. (SJ)

title: Moors SC spoil SSC’s bid for a memorable Major Club come back | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:44
-     - 6

Milan Rathnayaka struck early blows with three wickets to have SSC on the back foot

Ramesh Mendis held the Moors SC innings together with 85

SSC’s Prabath Jayasuriya celebrates a wicket on his way to a four-wicket haul

Nipun Dananjaya played a lone hand for SSC with 98

Induwara Udena ran through the SSC middle and lower order taking four wickets

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Moors SC led by Pasindu Sooriyabandara pulled off a memorable 25-run win over SSC to crown themselves champions in the Major Club 50-over tournament.

In the final played under lights at the R Premadasa Cricket Stadium yesterday, Moors SC invited to bat first ran up a decent total of 260 with the major part of their batting coming from the 79-run stand for the sixth wicket between Ramesh Mendis (85 off 91 balls, 5 fours, 1 six) and Milan Rathnayaka (43 off 61 balls, 2 fours, 2 sixes). Following Rathnayaka’s dismissal, Mendis carried on to take Moors SC to a total which they were to successfully defend.

The wickets for SSC were taken by their two left-arm bowlers – seamer Mihiranga Silva (3/36) and Prabath Jayasuriya (4/44).

Given the way SSC had scored in their previous matches leading up  to the final, the score was attainable with their strong batting line-up led by their captain Avishka Fernando who came into yesterday’s game with back to back hundreds (138 and 160) under his belt. But Rathnayaka showed how deadly he can be with the new ball. He struck thrice in his opening spell sending back Ron Chandraguptha (11), Avishka Fernando (6) and Nuwanidu Fernando (1) to have SSC reeling at 40-3.

It soon became 110-6 when the spinners came into play. Nipun Dananjaya (98 off 112 balls, 8 fours, 1 six) and Kavindu Nadeeshan (44 off 53 balls, 4 fours) mounted a counter attack with a partnership of 94 for the seventh wicket. But left-arm spinner Induwara Udena (4/44) not only got rid of both batsmen but kept the SSC run rate in check with some tidy bowling. With the asking rate mounting to over 10 an over the tail found it extremely difficult to find the boundaries and SSC were eventually dismissed for 235.

Despite the loss it was a good comeback to the Major Club fold by SSC and reach a final. They were relegated to Tier B following an indifferent 2024-25 season where they finished at the bottom two of their group in the Major Club 3-day league, but made a determined bid in 2025 to regain their lost prestige. They won the Tier B 50-over final beating Moratuwa SC by four wickets and made giant strides towards gaining promotion to the Major Club division by winning the Tier B 3-day league and finishing runner-up to Malay CC in the Tier B T20 final.

Scores:

 Moors SC 260 (49.5) (Sithara Gimhan 39, Sohan de Livera 29, Ramesh Mendis 85, Milan Rathnayaka 43, Mihiranga Silva 3/36, Prabath Jayasuriya 4/44) beat SSC 235 (49.5) (Dinura Kalupahana 30, Nipun Dananjaya 98, Kavindu Nadeeshan 44, Milan Rathnayaka 3/33, Induwara Udena 4/44)

title: Notice of injunction issued to SLC Transformation Committee | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:43
-     - 7

A notice of injunction was delivered by the Colombo District Magistrates Court yesterday against the Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee from attempting to reduce the number of participating teams in the Major Club tournament from 14 to 10.

Badureliya CC had sought a notice of injunction against the reduction of teams as it violated Sri Lanka Cricket’s earlier decision to reduce the teams down to only 14.  

However, after the Transformation Committee took over they decided to reduce the number of teams in the Major Club tournaments to 10.

According to the new tournament rules the promotion and relegation of teams in the Major Club and Tier B will take place on the weightage of points taken from all three formats – 3-day league, 50-over and T20.

On their performances so far in the two Major tournaments conducted thus far, Badureliya CC have finished at the bottom of their group in the Major Club 50-over without a single win, and in the Major Club T20 tournament they ended up sixth out of seven teams in their group which puts them in danger of relegation to Tier B with only the Major Club 3-day league tournament yet to be played.   

SLC Transformation Committee sources said they are confident that no restraining order will be given when the case is taken up again on 30 September.

By Shamseer Jaleel

St. Thomas’ College Mount Lavinia will host an exciting rugby tournament today (12 September), bringing together eight school teams for a full day of competitive action.

The participating teams have been divided into two groups. Group A comprises Wesley College, STC Mount, St. Anthony’s College and STC Bandarawela, while Group B consists of Thurstan College, St. Thomas’ Preparatory School, Isipathana College and Science College.

The tournament will commence at 9 a.m., with the opening encounter seeing Wesley take on STC Bandarawela. STC Mount will meet St. Anthony’s in the second game, followed by Thurstan against Science and St. Thomas’ Prep against Isipathana.

The group-stage matches will continue throughout the morning, with each team playing three games to determine the final group standings. The top two teams from each group will advance to the Cup quarter-finals, while the remaining sides will also have an opportunity to compete for the Plate.
